title: Measure the right result
brief: Configure the thrust–drag instrument so the engineering requirement can be decided.
supplied: Is 300 N available thrust sufficient against the modeled drag?

rho = 1.2 kg/m³
V = 30 m/s
S = 10 m²
Cd = 0.04 dimensionless
T = 300 N
Quasi-steady supplied coefficients. Change only the declared independent quantity; other inputs remain fixed.
This is a bounded teaching calculation. It does not establish aircraft safety, successful takeoff, or behavior outside the specified condition.
Greater speed reduces margin for constant thrust.
Compare available thrust with required drag at 30 and 40 m/s.
Show controls with units, supplied and student results separately, a result trace, and a clear limitation.

Supplied executable experiment recipe:
For each V in [20, 25, 30, 35, 40]:
  configured output = T-0.5*rho*V^2*S*Cd
  comparison = 0
Return the paired values with the declared units.

The app uses the arithmetic evaluator in src/core/onboarding/expression.js. It supports +, -, *, /, ^ and parentheses; it never evaluates an equation as JavaScript.
Retain the 30 m/s capacity claim; 40 m/s exceeds the constant available thrust.

checks.message: A capacity decision requires comparing supply and demand.
Nonnegative margin means thrust meets modeled drag.

hints: A reserve is the available quantity minus the demand.
Thrust and drag both have units of newtons; subtract drag from thrust.
Use thrust minus drag, N, and a zero minimum reserve.
